raw_response:
I am getting old, and there are only two of us at home, with some people working outside, so I cannot manage anything too troublesome. On 10.1 mu, I will still do wheat and then maize, same as the past years. That way is safer. Wheat gives me one harvest, maize gives me another, and if one side is not so good, the other can still bring something back. I have a well, so if the sky does not help, I can still water, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the crop really needs it.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too late, because late wheat never looks as strong. I will buy local wheat seed, the kind people around here use, nothing fancy. Before sowing I will put most of the fertilizer in, then after the wheat turns green and starts standing up in spring, I will add a bit more if the leaves look pale. I will water about three times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if the soil is dry, once around jointing, and once around grain filling. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest in June. That gap is very tight, so I will not do heavy tillage, just simple field prep and sow quickly. I will buy hybrid maize seed because saved maize seed is not reliable. Maize I will feed once at planting and once when it gets taller, and I will water once or twice depending on rain. I do not want to spend too much, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard, because if the crop goes yellow, the loss is bigger than the money saved.
